scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: You cut an onion, and within seconds your eyes sting and fill with tears. What is the onion doing to you?

scenes.name: cells
scenes.text: Cutting breaks open the onion's cells, mixing chemicals that are normally kept apart.

scenes.name: enzyme
scenes.text: Enzymes turn sulfur compounds into a new chemical, which quickly becomes a gas.

scenes.name: gas
scenes.text: This gas floats up into the air, and reaches your eyes.

scenes.name: sting
scenes.text: It irritates nerves in your eyes, and the brain tells your tear glands to flush it out.

scenes.name: defence
scenes.text: This is the onion's defence, to discourage animals from eating it.

scenes.name: tips
scenes.text: A sharp knife crushes fewer cells, and chilling the onion slows the reaction, so you cry less.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Cut cells, make gas, trigger tears. Follow for more on how things really work.
